similarity_meaning_lunar_base.text: Each Earth point is paired with its lunar twin: the 1-degree cell, among NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole, that holds the same thermal position and has a similar terrain. The coldest temperature and the daily temperature swing are compared as positions: where the point ranks among Earth's lunar-base candidates against where its twin ranks among the cells of the nine regions, each within 10 percentile points; the two places are not equally cold and the real values are far apart. Slope and roughness are compared in real values (the twin within 4 degrees and 60 m). The real values on both sides and their differences are shown next to every pair.
similarity_meaning_lunar_base.where: lunar_base (percentile_and_real_tolerance rule): wherever a similarity is shown, next to each variable's percentile on both sides (earth_lunar_base_pairs.bin '<variable>.earth_pct', '.moon_pct', '.diff_pct') and the real values and differences ('<variable>.earth', '.moon', '.diff', 'info.<variable>.*')

lunar_base_pair_sentence.text: This pair matches by relative thermal position, not by equal temperatures: this site's coldest temperature and daily swing rank among Earth's lunar-base candidates where its twin's rank among the cells of NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole. In real values the twin is {temp_diff_k} K colder on average (minimum {tmin_moon_c} °C at the surface against {tmin_earth_c} °C air temperature here) and its day-night swing is {amp_diff_k} K larger; slope differs by {slope_diff}° and roughness by {rough_diff} m.

temp_diff_k.meaning: mean temperature, Earth minus twin, in K (the twin is colder on every pair: checked by a test)

tmin_moon_c.meaning: the twin's coldest SURFACE temperature (Diviner, measured), K converted to degrees C

tmin_earth_c.meaning: the Earth point's coldest AIR temperature (WorldClim, modelled), K converted to degrees C

amp_diff_k.meaning: daily temperature swing, twin minus Earth, in K (the twin's is larger on every pair: checked by a test)

external_validation_lunar_base.text: What was checked against known places: 13 stations and analog field sites used for space research in cold, high or thermally harsh places, and 7 warm, humid tropical stations as a contrast. Of the 13, 3 pass the Lunar base funnel and 2 have a twin; in the ranking of 450 paired points they are Mars Desert Research Station (MDRS) (number 335) and Craters of the Moon National Monument (number 179). Passing without a twin: Black Point Lava Flow and SP Mountain (San Francisco Volcanic Field) (passes, but finds no twin among the cells of NASA's nine candidate regions). The other sites do not pass the funnel: Concordia Station (Dome C) (no value of daily land-surface temperature swing), Haughton impact crater (Devon Island, Nunavut) (daily land-surface temperature swing below 15), McMurdo Dry Valleys (no value of daily land-surface temperature swing), Svalbard - Bockfjorden volcanic complex (Sverrefjell) (daily land-surface temperature swing below 15, thermal-inertia class not allowed), Kangerlussuaq (ice-sheet margin) (daily land-surface temperature swing below 15), Mauna Kea - Pu'u Hiwahine (PISCES site) (coldest temperature above 5), Teide National Park - Minas de San Jose (Tenerife) (land share of the cell below 0.3, daily land-surface temperature swing below 15, coldest temperature above 5, thermal-inertia class not allowed), Iceland - Askja caldera (daily land-surface temperature swing below 15), Lanzarote - Timanfaya lava fields (land share of the cell below 0.3, coldest temperature above 5, thermal-inertia class not allowed) and Neumayer III / EDEN ISS greenhouse (no value of daily land-surface temperature swing, elevation below 1, land share of the cell below 0.3, thermal-inertia class not allowed). The recognised polar stations are analogs of cold and isolation, not of a large daily temperature swing, so the 15 K swing gate removes them. Of the 7 tropical stations, 0 pass the funnel. The check describes the ranking, it does not prove it.

zone_edge_lunar_base.text: The Lunar base zone includes every 1-degree lunar cell that touches one of NASA's nine candidate regions (280 cells), so a twin may lie mostly outside the region nearest to it: 69 of the 103 Lunar base twins have less than 50 % of their cell inside a region. Beside each twin we print either 'in NASA's ... candidate region' (50 % or more of the twin's cell lies inside that region) or 'at the edge of NASA's ... candidate region' (less than 50 %), naming the region its cell overlaps most.

Without it, Earth cells with a swing of about 1 K (for example on Ellesmere Island) would match the Moon's coldest temperature at a similarity of about 99, and the key variable, the thermal swing, would carry no weight in practice. The recognised polar stations therefore do not pass: daily land-surface swing Haughton crater (Devon Island) 2.5 K; Svalbard, Bockfjorden 1.2 K; Kangerlussuaq, ice-sheet margin 6.6 K; McMurdo and Concordia have no land-surface temperature in the table. They are analogs of cold and isolation, not of thermal cycling.

lunar_base_criteria.decision: 2026-11-15 11:28, 11:36 and 11:51 CET (the team lead, through his delegate; docs/DECISIONS.md 'Decisiones de las 11:28 y 11:36')
lunar_base_criteria.text: The Lunar base suitability uses one criterion for the ground instead of two: the bare-or-sparse fraction (from ESA CCI land cover, continuous, without the urban class) weighs 25 %; the thermal-inertia class (built from the same land-cover classes) and the permafrost class (modelled, missing on 607 of 2,419 passing points, with no sourced link to a base) carry no weight. The thermal-inertia class is still required and still excludes water. The four weights left (daily temperature swing 35 %, coldest temperature 25 %, bare-or-sparse fraction 25 %, ground sunlight 10 %) sum to 95 %, and the suitability is divided by that sum, so in effect they weigh 36.8 %, 26.3 %, 26.3 % and 10.5 %.

known_limitations: The Lunar base criteria are an exact copy of the team's thermal block (team design values, no external source). The ice block is shown per Earth cell as information only (passes or not, its suitability) and never changes this ranking; no lunar cell passes ice because the lunar permafrost class is the MODELLED label 'none', which the ice gate excludes.

Similarity is a likeness of thermal POSITION and real terrain, not of temperature (team decision of 2026-11-15 08:55 CET): the coldest temperature and the daily temperature swing are compared as percentiles within each population (Earth: the points passing this mission's funnel; Moon: the cells of NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole), each within 10 percentile points, and slope and roughness in real values (within 4 deg and 60 m). Equal positions do not mean equal temperatures: on every pair the twin is far colder and swings far more than the Earth point, and the real values and differences are shown with every pair. A point with no such cell keeps its suitability but has no twin, no similarity and no final score.

The coldest temperature is a MODELLED air temperature on Earth (WorldClim, coldest month, interpolated) and a MEASURED surface temperature on the Moon (Diviner night minimum); the Earth diurnal amplitude is a difference between two satellite overpasses and understates the daily range. Both are suitability criteria on Earth, and in the similarity only their position within each population is compared, never their values.
Antarctica has no land surface temperature product here, so its cells fail for lack of a daily temperature swing value ('no data').

The list is ordered by the final score: 50 % similarity to the lunar twin and 50 % suitability for the mission. These are five of the highest-scoring analogs in our model, not a proven best: the five best final scores once a cell half or more snow and ice, a cell less than half land and a point within 2 degrees of one already chosen are skipped (numbers 1, 3, 5, 6 and 7 of the full ranking).

How stable these five are: under the documented uncertainty of the input data (200 simulations), number 1 stays in the top 5 in 18.0 % of the simulations and in the top 20 in 51.5 %; number 2 stays in the top 5 in 23.0 % of the simulations and in the top 20 in 52.5 %; number 3 stays in the top 5 in 19.0 % of the simulations and in the top 20 in 43.5 %; number 4 stays in the top 5 in 18.0 % of the simulations and in the top 20 in 38.0 %; number 5 stays in the top 5 in 22.5 % of the simulations and in the top 20 in 59.0 %. The same five come back together in 0 of the 200 simulations. Under a change of plus or minus 10 % in any one weight, number 1 stays in the top 5 in 16 of the 16 weight changes, number 2 in 16, number 3 in 15, number 4 in 15 and number 5 in 10. The five are a sample of close candidates, not a fixed answer.

The Lunar base keeps the team's gate 'daily thermal swing at least 15 K'. Without it, Earth cells with a swing of about 1 K (for example on Ellesmere Island) would match the Moon's coldest temperature at a similarity of about 99, and the key variable, the thermal swing, would carry no weight in practice. The recognised polar stations therefore do not pass: daily land-surface swing Haughton crater (Devon Island) 2.5 K; Svalbard, Bockfjorden 1.2 K; Kangerlussuaq, ice-sheet margin 6.6 K; McMurdo and Concordia have no land-surface temperature in the table. They are analogs of cold and isolation, not of thermal cycling.

The Lunar base suitability uses one criterion for the ground instead of two: the bare-or-sparse fraction (from ESA CCI land cover, continuous, without the urban class) weighs 25 %; the thermal-inertia class (built from the same land-cover classes) and the permafrost class (modelled, missing on 607 of 2,419 passing points, with no sourced link to a base) carry no weight. The thermal-inertia class is still required and still excludes water. The four weights left (daily temperature swing 35 %, coldest temperature 25 %, bare-or-sparse fraction 25 %, ground sunlight 10 %) sum to 95 %, and the suitability is divided by that sum, so in effect they weigh 36.8 %, 26.3 %, 26.3 % and 10.5 %.
